cases.case_title: RML Hospital Delhi recalls 10 NSQ/defective drug batches from own stock (Glowson India Labs tablets found as powder; some samples supplied by Jackson Laboratories)
cases.agency: Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital, New Delhi - inventory management section, oral and topical drug unit and injectable drug unit (four recall notices dated 7, 9 and 14 Sep 2026, two on 14 Sep). No police, Delhi Drugs Control or CDSCO action on this recall reported in any opened page.
cases.fir_details: not reported
cases.seizure_value_inr: not applicable (hospital quality recall, no seizure)
cases.hospital_link: Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital (Centre-run), New Delhi - affected batches were in the hospital's own stock; departments and wards were directed to stop use and return stock to the designated drug units (NSQ batches by 18 Sep 2026; the two powder-defect tablet batches within three days of the notice). Hospital says interim arrangements made for alternative medicines and no severe adverse effect reported by end users. Note: NSQ/physical-defect recall, not a counterfeit bust.
cases.status: 10 batches recalled via four hospital notices (7-14 Sep 2026): 8 failed analytical testing (NSQ), 2 found as powder in strips. Hospital 'initiated the recall process and issued recall letters', told units to report any patient-related problems; no severe adverse effects reported; situation 'being closely monitored'. No FIR, licence action or CDSCO/Delhi Drugs Control follow-up on this recall reported as of 4 Oct 2026. Separately, Jackson Laboratories Pvt Ltd (named by RML officials as supplier of 'some samples') had the manufacturing licences of its Punjab and Himachal Pradesh units cancelled by state licensing authorities after CDSCO/state joint inspections in June 2026, amid the Rajasthan oxytocin maternal-deaths probe (unrelated to the RML recall).

cases.case_title: Kerala scraps KMSCL quality control wing after substandard medicines worth crores reached govt hospitals; quality testing shifted to State Drugs Control Department and procurement overhaul ordered
cases.agency: Kerala Government (Health and Devaswom Minister K. Muraleedharan) / Kerala Medical Services Corporation Limited (KMSCL); quality testing of all KMSCL-procured medicines transferred to the Kerala State Drugs Control Department
cases.fir_details: not reported (administrative action; no FIR, police station or sections mentioned on any opened page)
cases.seizure_value_inr: not a seizure case; pages state medicines 'worth crores of rupees' procured and distributed through KMSCL were found substandard (no exact figure given)
cases.hospital_link: YES - KMSCL procures and distributes medicines to all Kerala government hospitals and other government institutions; pages state medicines 'procured and distributed through KMSCL' were found substandard. No individual recipient hospital is named. Government Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram (its in-house drug bank) is named only as a price benchmark for future KMSCL procurement, not as a recipient of substandard drugs.
cases.status: Ongoing administrative overhaul. 2026-09-10: KMSCL Quality Control wing dismantled; State Drugs Control Department to inspect/test all KMSCL-procured medicines before distribution to government hospitals; temporary contract staff sanctioned for the department; Minister wrote to Principal Secretary (Health). 2026-09-22: KMSCL board noted no bidders for 180 tender items and higher prices for 171 items; decided to procure 25% additional stock of costlier items from existing suppliers and re-tender the rest; government hospitals facing shortages (paracetamol, antibiotics, chemotherapy drugs, IV fluids etc.); purchase orders placed end of August. 2026-09-26: Minister ordered procurement overhaul - tender for next year's purchases to begin October 2026, complete by December, medicines available by February; middlemen completely excluded from tender process and barred from KMSCL premises; pharmaceutical companies to participate directly; authorised direct agencies allowed for imported medicines; companies charging exorbitant prices excluded; medicines supplied to the government sector in at least two states eligible; KMSCL to procure below Government Medical College Thiruvananthapuram in-house drug bank prices and publish annual procurement prices on its website; companies supplying any batch of substandard medicines to be permanently blacklisted. No supplier names, batch numbers, FIRs, arrests or licence actions reported.
firms: suppliers not named on any opened page (review found 'several companies that received purchase orders from KMSCL in February manufacture certain medicines exclusively for the corporation' - names not disclosed)

products.issue: NSQ/substandard medicines procured and distributed through KMSCL ('medicines worth crores of rupees'); no brand, batch or manufacturer disclosed
products.original_manufacturer: not reported

cases.enrichment: New facts added from opened pages: exact timeline (QC wing scrapped Thursday 2026-09-10; The Hindu published 2026-09-10 08:16 pm IST; Onmanorama 2026-09-10; Medical Dialogues 2026-09-11; overhaul order 2026-09-26). Minister's full designation: Health and Devaswom Minister K. Muraleedharan; he wrote to the Principal Secretary (Health). Temporary contract staff sanctioned for the Drugs Control Department due to personnel shortage. Overhaul details (2026-09-26): tender process for next year's purchases to begin October 2026, completed by December, medicines available by February; middlemen barred from tender process and from KMSCL premises or receiving any gratification; pharmaceutical companies to participate directly; authorised direct agencies for imported medicines; medicines supplied to the government sector in at least two states eligible for procurement; KMSCL to procure below the in-house drug bank prices of Government Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram and publish annual procurement prices on its website; review found several companies that received KMSCL purchase orders in February manufacture certain medicines exclusively for the corporation; KMSCL General Manager said fever medicines and antibiotics in stock. Supply-crisis context (2026-09-22, Kozhikode report): KMSCL board found no bidders for 180 tender items and higher prices for 171 items; 25% additional stock of costlier items bought from existing suppliers; re-tendering and quality checks incomplete; shortages of aspirin, omeprazole, metformin, doxycycline, paracetamol, carboplatin, cisplatin, IDRV (rabies vaccine), acyclovir, amoxicillin, DEC tablets, atorvastatin, albendazole, IV fluids; GM post changed hands twice; Food Safety Commissioner given additional charge as KMSCL MD. No batch numbers, supplier/manufacturer names, hospital names, FIR numbers, arrests, chargesheets, bail or licence actions were disclosed on any opened page. Four new source URLs appended.

cases.case_title: Delhi Crime Branch (Inter-State Cell) busts Rs 9 crore counterfeit/diverted anti-cancer drug syndicate; 17 arrested incl. hospital oncology nursing staff; govt supply for PBM Hospital Bikaner diverted
cases.state: Delhi (network across Delhi-NCR, Uttar Pradesh [Ghaziabad/Noida], Haryana [Gurugram/Faridabad/Jhajjar], Maharashtra [Navi Mumbai], Telangana [Hyderabad], Rajasthan [Alwar; govt supply diverted from Bikaner] - reported as '7 states')
cases.city: Delhi (Laxmi Nagar, Govindpuri; raids in East Delhi, Rohini) with nodes in Navi Mumbai, Hyderabad, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad (Indirapuram, Raj Nagar Extension), Noida, Jhajjar, Alwar
cases.agency: Delhi Police Crime Branch, Inter-State Cell (DCP Crime Branch Aditya Gautam); raids with Drugs Department and local police; Rajasthan Health Minister Gajendra Singh Khinvsar ordered a state probe; Delhi Police sought procurement/batch/distribution records from RMSCL and PBM Hospital management
cases.fir_details: FIR registered on 2026-07-12 at Police Station Crime Branch, Delhi under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (FIR number and specific sections not published). Timeline: secret input received 2026-06-22; seven Inter-State Cell teams raided Delhi and Navi Mumbai simultaneously on 2026-07-11; bust announced 2026-08-20.
cases.seizure_value_inr: approx Rs 9 crore: 588 filled anti-cancer vials, 6 empty vials, 7 empty medicine boxes, 3,021 units of other medicines; plus approx Rs 50 lakh cash, electronic devices, registers, diaries, packaging material (thermocol boxes, bubble rolls, adhesive tape, polythene). Per-accused recoveries: Anand Kumar 337 vials + large quantity of other medicines; Deepak alias Ravi 108 vials + Rs 6.50 lakh; Mayank Garg 55 vials; Srinivasulu Kalva 23 suspected fake vials; Mukesh 12 vials + Rs 16.50 lakh (from vehicle); Paramjeet Sheoran 9 vials (from medical store); Manish Sharma 5 filled + 4 empty vials; Shubham Kumar Chaudhary Rs 23 lakh; Abhishek Vaishya Rs 4 lakh. (ETV Bharat English 2026-08-20 early report cited 22 vials each worth over Rs 1 lakh and Rs 27.19 lakh cash.)
cases.hospital_link: YES - hospital employees among the 17 accused: Jaswant Sharma (42, Faridabad), nursing-qualified oncology department nursing in-charge of a 'reputed hospital' (name not disclosed), allegedly removed anti-cancer vials from the hospital and passed them to Deepak alias Ravi (33, Faridabad), a dental technician and former personal assistant to an oncologist at the same hospital; Manish Sharma (28, Alwar, Rajasthan), nursing-qualified, recently joined a hospital, allegedly misappropriated injections kept for patients; Malugari Srinath Reddy (35, Hyderabad), B Pharma-qualified employee of a 'reputed hospital', allegedly supplied medicines meant for patients; Ramdas Satish Kumar (42, Hyderabad), former worker at a reputed hospital, allegedly misappropriated medicines; Srinivasulu Kalva (52, Hyderabad medical store owner) allegedly received drugs from a hospital; Mayank Garg and Mukesh allegedly sourced drugs from hospitals via hospital staff. Hospital names NOT disclosed by police. Government supply: at least four of the confiscated vials were traced to a government consignment meant for the Acharya Tulsi Regional Cancer Research Institute at PBM Hospital, Bikaner (Rajasthan); govt-supply markings had been erased; Thar Express (2026-08-27) reports batch numbers of the fake injections seized in Delhi matched medicines missing from the Bikaner government cancer hospital; RMSCL CMD Pukhraj Sen said RMSCL had safely supplied the medicine to the hospital and hospital administration claims the medicines were administered to patients. Yahoo/Independent: syndicate traded stolen and fake drugs 'from several government hospitals' and theft of vials/packaging from private hospitals.
cases.status: 17 arrested (announced 2026-08-20); investigation continuing to trace supply/financial network, end beneficiaries and role of other persons and business entities; further arrests expected; Rajasthan government inquiry ordered; Merck lab (Germany) test via manufacturer found avelumab (Bavencio) vials sold at ~Rs 1 lakh contained zero active ingredient (only water; Thar Express: water and bacteria). No chargesheet, bail or licence action reported on any opened page as of 2026-10-04 (ETV Bharat: probe still ongoing in all three Delhi cancer-drug cases).

cases.fir_details: No FIR, police station or IPC/BNS sections reported in any opened page. Action has been administrative/regulatory: Punjab FDA licence cancellation order dated 3 June 2026 (recall of all products manufactured since 25 April 2023, destruction of stocks within 14 days under the zonal licensing authority, Amritsar); Rajasthan ADC Devendra Garg order dated 23 June 2026 cancelling wholesale licence of Messer Rajasthan Medical Hall (inspection 19 May 2026, show-cause notice 21 May 2026). TOI (28 Jun and 8 Jul 2026): company moved a Kota court seeking retesting; Rajasthan sent samples to a Kolkata drug-testing laboratory and 'proposed prosecution will remain on hold until the fresh report is received'; legal proceedings to be initiated if the batch fails again. Jan Swasthya Abhiyan demanded FIRs; NHRC complaint seeks criminal action.
cases.seizure_value_inr: Rajasthan drug control seized about 3,500 vials of TOCIN batch I-7881 (TOI/Outlook); IANS breakdown: 2,479 injections from Kota Medical College store (estimated value about Rs 25,000), 72 from J.K. Lon Hospital, nearly 950 held by the supplier; ETV Bharat: 16,000 injections supplied to the two hospitals, 3,501 seized, 12,499 already used, total cost estimated around Rs 1.60 lakh
cases.hospital_link: Government hospitals in Kota supplied with TOCIN batch I-7881 via local purchase from distributor Rajasthan Medical Hall: Government New Medical College Hospital (NMCH) / Super Speciality Wing of Government Medical College, Kota, and J.K. Lon (JK Lone) Hospital, Kota (ETV Bharat: 'These injections were supplied to both hospitals'; hospital superintendent Dr. Ashutosh Sharma said the defective injections were in the medical college's rate contract and were administered at both the medical college and JK Lon). Five women died 5-17 May 2026 after caesarean sections: Payal (New Medical Hospital, Kota, May 5), Jyoti (May 7), Priya Mahawar (J.K. Lon Hospital, Kota, May 9), Pinki Mahawar (May 10), Shireen (New Medical Hospital, Kota, May 17) (MedPath/The Federal). Two further deaths at PBM Hospital, Bikaner (Preeti, June 19; Sharda Nayak, June 21) and eight women with kidney impairment/septicemia after C-sections at a district hospital in Jodhpur were reported; Jackson Labs' rejoinder says its product 'was never used' in Bikaner, Jodhpur, Nagaur, Bhilwara and Banswara. ADC Garg said the injections had reportedly been administered to nearly 12,500 women over four months. Causation disputed: Rajasthan government attributes deaths to multiple factors; gynaecologist Ritika Mathur and ADC Garg said the injection was unlikely to directly cause death; one deceased (Shirin) reportedly was not given the injection. Survivors on dialysis named in IANS report: Ragini Meena, Aarti, Dhanni, Pinky, Sushila.
cases.status: Confirmed: Rajasthan DTL Jaipur found batch I-7881 contains no oxytocin (CDSCO May-2026 alert); RDTL Chandigarh and DTL Delhi failed the same batch on identification (CDSCO Jul-2026 alert). Rajasthan banned sale/use of the batch (25 May 2026), seized stock, issued statewide alert and recall. Punjab FDA cancelled Jackson Laboratories' Amritsar manufacturing licence and product permissions by order of 3 June 2026 with nationwide recall of all products made since 25 April 2023 (Mint 4 Jun 2026; ET 27 Jun 2026). Himachal Pradesh cancelled the Baddi unit licence in June 2026 after CDSCO joint inspection (ET/TOI/Medical Dialogues 26-29 Jun 2026); Baddi licence partially restored with sterile injectables, testosterone injection, etophylline/theophylline PR tablets and other high-risk lines still halted (ET 1 Aug 2026); Punjab licence remains cancelled, company filed rejoinder through advocate Sanjay Kumar Jain seeking revocation, appeal before state health secretary listed for 14 August 2026 (ET 24 Jul and 31 Jul 2026) - outcome not found. Company moved a Kota court for retesting; samples sent to Kolkata lab; prosecution on hold pending that report (TOI 28 Jun, 8 Jul 2026). Distributor Messer Rajasthan Medical Hall, Kota wholesale licence cancelled 23 June 2026. WHO sought information via DCGI; Rajasthan submitted factual report. Om Birla handed Rs 5 lakh cheques to the five families (11 Jul 2026). NHRC directed Rajasthan to act within eight weeks (31 Jul 2026). Three suspended Kota Medical College doctors (Dr. B.L. Patidar, Dr. Khushbu Meena, Dr. Navneet Kumar) reinstated after four enquiry committees found no negligence; nine medical-device samples sent to Kolkata lab still awaited (IANS/Punjab Kesari 5 Oct 2026). No FIR, arrest or chargesheet reported. Company blacklisted earlier in Karnataka, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and J&K per reports. Separate NSQ: Dinoprostone gel batch H-084 from a Roorkee firm (not Jackson) also failed.

cases.seizure_value_inr: Rs 200 crore of fake medicines, raw materials and machinery seized by Puducherry CBCID in the original case (Dinamalar; countryandpolitics); Agra leg: counterfeit medicines worth approx Rs 7.1 crore seized from five Agra firms, counterfeit medicines and machinery worth nearly Rs 30 crore (incl. a packaging machine valued ~Rs 20 crore) at Rana's Puducherry unit, and Rs 5 crore in CDSCO raids on two linked factories in Sept 2025 (The420); CBI/agencies describe the racket as Rs 5,000 crore (BW Police World, Global Governance News, DT Next); Rs 10,000 crore figure appears only in countryandpolitics. cases.case_title: Coldrif cough syrup (Sresan Pharmaceutical, Kancheepuram TN) DEG contamination 48.6% w/v, batch SR-13; child deaths in Chhindwara MP; 7 arrests, TN licence cancelled, ED PMLA attachment, MP HC bail refused
cases.city: Sunguvarchatraam (Mathura), Kancheepuram; Chennai (Kodambakkam); Parasia/Chhindwara, Betul, Pandhurna (MP); Nagpur (treatment)
cases.agency: Madhya Pradesh Police SIT (Chhindwara; SIT in-charge/Parasia SDOP Jitendra Kumar Jaat; SP Ajay Pandey); Parasia court (Chhindwara); Madhya Pradesh High Court (Jabalpur); Tamil Nadu Drugs Control Department (NSQ report 2 Oct 2025, licence cancellation, unit sealed, two drug inspectors suspended); Govt Drug Testing Laboratory Bhopal; MP FDA (Controller Food & Drugs Administration MP - ban order, recall); CDSCO/DCGI (risk-based inspections in 6 states; DCGI letter 7 Oct 2025); Union Health Ministry/DGHS (advisory); Enforcement Directorate Chennai Zonal Office (PMLA searches, provisional attachment); Chennai ACB (corruption FIR against TN drugs control official); WHO (Medical Product Alert N5/2025, 13 Oct 2025); expert panel NIV, ICMR-NEERI, CDSCO, AIIMS Nagpur
cases.fir_details: FIR registered early Sunday 5 Oct 2025 at Parasia police station, Chhindwara district, MP, on complaint of Dr Ankit Sahlam, Block Medical Officer, Community Health Centre Parasia, under Sections 105 and 276 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 27(a) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; named: directors of Sresan Pharmaceuticals, Dr Praveen Soni of Parasia and 'other responsible persons'. FIR number not reported. MP High Court order of 17 Feb 2026 records offences under D&C Act s.27(A) and BNS ss.105, 276 and 238(b). ED (PMLA) proceeds on two scheduled-offence FIRs: the MP Police FIR under BNS s.105 against G. Ranganathan, Proprietor M/s Sresan Pharmaceutical Manufacturer, and a Chennai ACB FIR against P.U. Karthigeyan, Director (i/c) and Joint Director of Drugs Control, Tamil Nadu, under s.7 Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018. FIR cites TN Director of Drugs Control lab report dated 2 Oct 2025 (48.6% DEG) and Govt Drug Testing Laboratory Bhopal (46.28%) and kidney biopsy of victim Vikas Yaduvanshi (4) at GMC Nagpur. Drug Inspector Jabalpur also instructed to lodge FIR (none registered as of 5 Oct 2025). Ranganathan produced before Parasia court 10 Oct 2025 and remanded to 10-day police custody.
cases.seizure_value_inr: ED provisionally attached immovable properties worth approx. Rs 2.04 crore (two residential flats at Kodambakkam, Chennai owned by G Ranganathan and family) under PMLA, reported 4 Dec 2025. Approx. 660 bottles of Coldrif sold in Chhindwara area, most recovered (MPFDA); 594 bottles earlier reported distributed to three local distributors; 66 bottles allegedly destroyed by accused pharmacist (MP HC order).
cases.hospital_link: Children (all under 5) were prescribed the syrup by Dr Praveen Soni, a government paediatrician posted at Civil Hospital/CHC Parasia, during private practice at his clinic in Parasia; syrup dispensed from M/s Apna Medical Store, Parasia (owned by Jyoti Soni, wife of Dr Soni) where Coldrif was dispensed in place of prescribed Nextro-DS without bills; some children also seen by Dr Aman Siddiqui and Dr Amit Thakur. Children were treated at Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) Nagpur (10 of the first 11 deaths occurred there; kidney biopsy of Vikas Yaduvanshi done at GMC Nagpur) and AIIMS Nagpur (two MP children critical, Oct 2025). No government hospital pharmacy purchase disclosed; MP FDA ordered stop of sale/distribution of Coldrif and all other Sresan products and recall; Coldrif banned in TN, MP, Kerala, Karnataka, Punjab, HP, UP, Puducherry, West Bengal and Delhi.
cases.status: Seven arrested: G. Ranganathan (owner, arrested 8-9 Oct 2025 at Chennai by MP SIT, Rs 20,000 reward had been announced; 10-day police custody by Parasia court 10 Oct 2025); Dr Praveen Soni (arrested ~5 Oct 2025, suspended by MP Health Commissioner Tarun Rathi); chemist K Maheshwari, wholesaler Rajesh Soni, medical store pharmacist Sourabh Jain and Sresan medical representative Satish Verma (Verma arrested night of 26-27 Oct 2025 at Chhindwara); Jyoti Soni (medical shop proprietor, arrested 3 Nov 2025 at Parasia). MP High Court (Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal, order 17 Feb 2026) dismissed regular bail of the pharmacist (in custody since 13 Oct 2025), Dr Praveen Soni, Jyoti Soni and nephew. TN Drugs Control cancelled Sresan's manufacturing licence and shut the company (Monday 13 Oct 2025), unit sealed, two senior drug inspectors suspended; ED searched 7 Chennai locations incl. Ranganathan's Kodambakkam residence and Drug Control offices (13 Oct 2025; 10 locations in all per ED) and provisionally attached Rs 2.04 crore assets (4 Dec 2025). MP suspended its drug controller and assistant drug controller. Death toll: 20 (8 Oct 2025: 17 Chhindwara, 2 Betul, 1 Pandhurna), 22-23 by mid-Oct, 24 by late Oct 2025, 'more than 26' per MP HC Feb 2026; 2-3 deaths in Rajasthan. MP CM Mohan Yadav announced Rs 4 lakh ex gratia per deceased child and free treatment. WHO Medical Product Alert N5/2025 (13 Oct 2025); DGHS advisory against cough/cold syrups for children under 2; DCGI letter 7 Oct 2025 on testing raw materials/excipients; CDSCO risk-based inspections in HP, Uttarakhand, Gujarat, TN, MP, Maharashtra. IAP/IMA protested Dr Soni's arrest. Sresan's Respolite-D syrup flagged NSQ (content) by DTL Madurai in CDSCO Dec 2025 list. Chargesheet not reported on any opened page; trial pending; ongoing.

cases.agency: West Bengal government / Health Dept (stop-manufacture order on Paschim Banga Pharmaceutical; prohibition on use of its RL in medical facilities on 14 Jan 2025; 13-member inquiry committee; preliminary report pointing to human error reviewed by the CM; 12 Midnapore MCH doctors suspended; CID probe ordered); West Bengal CID (parallel probe ordered ~13 Jan 2025); Calcutta High Court (asked the Bengal health dept why banned Paschim Banga RL stocks were not withdrawn after the stop-manufacture order, reported 16 Jan 2025); Karnataka Health Department (wrote to DCGI seeking action against M/s. Paschim Banga Pharmaceuticals and an investigation into the Standard Quality certification issued by Central Drugs Laboratory, Kolkata, after Ballari District Hospital maternal deaths); CDSCO monthly NSQ alerts (CDL Kolkata, RDTL Guwahati, State Lab Karnataka)
cases.fir_details: No FIR number, police station or sections found on any opened page. TOI (11 Jan 2025, via RSS mirror) reports the woman's husband and other affected families filed complaints alleging negligence; TOI (16 Jan 2025) reports 12 doctors suspended and a CID probe ordered. No FIR or arrest against the manufacturer reported on any opened page.
cases.seizure_value_inr: not reported (regulatory/NSQ action; no seizure value published)
cases.hospital_link: Midnapore Medical College & Hospital (Midnapore Medical College Hospital / MMCH), West Bengal: a 22-year-old woman died and four others were critically ill after C-sections (TOI 11 Jan 2025); families blamed expired Ringer's lactate IV solution; 13-member committee formed; preliminary report suggested human error over Ringer's Lactate, with three other women still critical (TOI 13 Jan 2025); 12 MMCH doctors suspended and CID probe ordered; Calcutta HC asked why Paschim Banga Pharmaceutical RL stocks were not withdrawn after the stop-manufacture order (TOI 16 Jan 2025); RL saline from Paschim Banga Pharmaceuticals prohibited in medical facilities on 14 January (currentaffair mirror, 22 Jan 2025, which also describes the death as of 'a woman and her newborn child' - not corroborated by the TOI items). Ballari District Hospital, Karnataka: Paschim Banga RL was used in the hospital during a series of maternal deaths; Karnataka Health Dept wrote to DCGI seeking action against the manufacturer and an investigation into CDL Kolkata's Standard Quality certification (The Hindu, Afshan Yasmeen). Assam Medical Services Corporation Ltd (Health and Family Welfare Department, Assam) empanelment tender 2023_HFWD_29257_1 (ref AMSCL/ECF/255581/150953): PASCHIM BANGA PHARMACEUTICAL (A Unit of Farista Vanijya Pvt. Ltd.) bidder no. 181378 shown as 'Accepted-AOC', L1, AOC dated 09-Nov-2023 - indicates government hospital supply chain in Assam (tender data only; delivery not verified).
cases.status: Manufacturing stopped by West Bengal stop-manufacture order (date not stated on opened pages); Paschim Banga RL prohibited in WB medical facilities from 14 Jan 2025; 12 Midnapore MCH doctors suspended; WB CID probe ordered; Calcutta HC hearing reported 16 Jan 2025 questioning non-withdrawal of stocks. Karnataka Health Dept sought DCGI action against the manufacturer. CDSCO continued to list the firm's batches as NSQ through Nov-2025, Apr-2026 and Aug-2026 alerts. No chargesheet, bail, arrest or formal licence cancellation/suspension order seen on any opened page; 'licence cancelled' remains unsupported. Search-result snippets (pages egress-blocked, not opened) additionally claim: Calcutta HC directed Paschim Banga Pharmaceuticals to halt all commercial production and the state to compensate victims' families (pharmacypro.io); Karnataka CM ordered suspension of the state drugs controller, blacklisting and prosecution of the company, and 22 RL batches failed testing (Deccan Herald / ETV Bharat); these are unverified.

cases.case_title: Ballari maternal deaths from NSQ Paschim Banga Ringer's Lactate (KSMSCL supply) - blacklisting, prosecutions, Lokayukta probe, West Bengal stop-manufacture order
cases.state: Karnataka (deaths, prosecutions) / West Bengal (manufacturer; stop-manufacture order; Midnapore death, Calcutta HC)
cases.city: Ballari (Ballari District Hospital; Ballari Institute of Medical Sciences / BIMS, formerly VIMS, also reported as Ballari Medical College and Research Centre); cases filed in Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Haveri, Bengaluru, Gadag and other districts; manufacturer at Chopra, Uttar Dinajpur, West Bengal
cases.agency: Karnataka Health & Family Welfare Dept (Principal Secretary Harsh Gupta letter to DCGI, 3 Dec 2024); Karnataka Drugs Control Dept / Drugs Testing Laboratory Karnataka (Government Analyst; district Drug Controllers filed court complaints 7-9 Dec 2024); KSMSCL; Karnataka Lokayukta (suo motu case 6 Dec 2024, Justice B S Patil; Lokayukta police SP Siddharaju C inspected Ballari hospitals 7 Dec 2024); RGUHS expert panel (Dr Savitha C); joint inspection by Karnataka, West Bengal and DCGI teams; West Bengal Directorate of Drugs Control, Siliguri regional office (stop-manufacture order 10 Dec 2024); Calcutta High Court (division bench CJ T S Sivagnanam and Justice Hiranmay Bhattacharyya, 16 Jan 2025); West Bengal CID (Midnapore death); CDSCO NSQ alerts via CDL Kolkata and RDTL Guwahati (2024-2026)
cases.fir_details: No police FIR number reported. Prosecution is by court complaints under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act: The Hindu (3 Dec 2024) reports 'a criminal case has been registered against the company'; The News Minute (20 Dec 2024) reports Drug Controllers of five districts - Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Haveri, Bengaluru and Gadag - filed complaints in jurisdictional courts between 7-9 Dec 2024, the Shivamogga case under Sections 18(a)(i) and 27(d) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act (1-2 years imprisonment, minimum fine Rs 20,000). The News Minute (14 Apr 2025): a government press release said 78 cases had been filed against Paschim Banga; TNM found 30 cases filed by the state in courts of 13 districts since Dec 2024, mostly under Sections 25(4), 18(a)(1) and 27(d) of the D&C Act. Karnataka Lokayukta registered a suo motu case on 6 Dec 2024 with 70 respondents including the Principal Secretary (Health & FW and Medical Education), the Drugs Controller and KSMSCL (Deccan Herald 20 Dec 2024; The South First 8 Dec 2024). Health Minister said the department was considering a criminal case against empanelled labs that cleared the drug (TOI 17 Dec 2024).
cases.seizure_value_inr: not reported (Lokayukta police seized a box of 25 bottles of batch 03BF2338 from Ballari for testing - Deccan Herald 20 Dec 2024)
cases.hospital_link: Ballari District Hospital (34-36 caesarean sections 9-11 Nov 2024; batch received 8 Nov 2024; RL issued by Ballari district drug warehouse without invoice/indent); Ballari Institute of Medical Sciences (BIMS, formerly VIMS; also called Ballari Medical College and Research Centre/BMCRC) where referred women died; Gudekote Primary Health Centre (Kudligi taluk) for the sixth woman T Mahalakshmi; Belagavi District Hospital warehouse where Lokayukta team found the same company's IV fluid, distributed to Belagavi hospitals since April 2024 (The Federal); all Karnataka government hospitals supplied via KSMSCL district drug warehouses (192-197 batches of RL procured); earlier adverse-reaction complaints from doctors in Gundlupet and Chitradurga (TOI); Midnapore Medical College and Hospital, West Bengal (death of Mamoni Ruidas on 10 Jan 2025 and others critical after RL from the same firm; ~30,000 units in WB state facilities). KSMSCL = Karnataka State Medical Supplies Corporation Ltd.
cases.status: Karnataka: CM Siddaramaiah on 30 Nov 2024 ordered suspension of State Drugs Controller Umesh S (Dr Umesh S) for dereliction of duty, blacklisting and prosecution of Paschim Banga Pharmaceuticals, departmental inquiry against the KSMSCL managing director, warning to the Ballari district surgeon; Rs 2 lakh compensation announced, later reported as Rs 5 lakh paid; IAS officer K Srinivas appointed to head Drugs Control Dept (The Federal). Principal Secretary Harsh Gupta wrote to DCGI on 3 Dec 2024 seeking investigation of CDL Kolkata's SQ certification and action against the manufacturer (licensed in Form 28D by WB Licensing Authority). KSMSCL had frozen all batches and blacklisted the firm in March 2024 (DH: 23 Mar 2024; Health Dept: two batches declared NSQ on 18 Mar 2024) after state-lab NSQ reports; the firm obtained a Karnataka High Court stay on the blacklisting in April 2024 and CDL Kolkata later certified challenged batches SQ; KSMSCL TAC unfroze 84-86 batches on 13/17 Aug 2024; all batches re-frozen 16 Nov 2024. Of 192-197 batches supplied, 92 were tested and 22 found NSQ (sterility, bacterial endotoxins, particulate matter); by April 2025 the Health Dept said 113 batches NSQ (DCD website listed 121). RGUHS panel ruled out medical negligence and blamed RL. Lokayukta preliminary probe (DH 20 Dec 2024): victims given batch 03BF2338, an unauthorised batch not on the de-frozen list, issued without invoice; full investigation launched, responses sought by 16 Jan 2025. Four labs (Devansh Testing Lab, Vimta, Standard Analytical and the government lab) found batch 03BF2338 passed sterility/particulate/BET tests (TNM Apr 2025), although the Health Minister told the Council on 17 Dec 2024 that the batch used did not meet safety standards. Court complaints filed by district Drug Controllers from 7 Dec 2024 (30-78 cases). Health Minister Dinesh Gundu Rao proposed a judicial commission (Dec 2024); statewide maternal-death audit (464 deaths Apr-Dec 2024 reviewed) and Maatrutva Suraksha Abhiyaan launched 21 Jan 2025. West Bengal: after joint Karnataka-WB-DCGI inspection, the WB Directorate of Drugs Control (Siliguri regional office) ordered the firm to stop manufacturing RL on 10 Dec 2024 (TOI 17 Dec 2024 / 17 Jan 2025); after Mamoni Ruidas died at Midnapore Medical College on 10 Jan 2025, WB ordered a CID probe, directed all hospitals on 14 Jan 2025 to stop using every medicine from the firm, and Calcutta HC on 16 Jan 2025 called the delay 'disturbing', directed state compensation to the family and reports from the Chief Secretary and central authorities; the company's lawyer said production of the solution had stopped. No licence cancellation, chargesheet, conviction or arrest reported in any opened page. CDSCO central-lab alerts continued to list the firm's RL as NSQ (03B3911 Nov-2025, 03BF2084 Apr-2026, 03BF2457 Aug-2026 - all batches manufactured 2023-2024). Ongoing.

cases.fir_details: FIR 1: lodged 29 July 2026 at Aminabad Police Station under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS); 5 named: Manish Mishra, Amod Kumar Mishra, Sunny Kashyap, Devendra Shukla, Rahul (Medical Dialogues 2 Aug 2026; ETV Bharat 30 Jul 2026 - Joint Commissioner Brajesh Kumar quoted). FIR 3 (follow-up): registered in Saharanpur after 2 Sept 2026 Nagal-area operation, naming Vineet Kumar, Pratish Kumar, Prem Malik, Ishtar Bhai, Rahman, Amit Sen, Ejaz and Ubair as an organised syndicate (India TV News 2 Sept). A separate Lucknow FIR was registered over two batches of Levera-500 found 'not genuine in nature' by the state laboratory (India TV News 2 Sept). FIR numbers not disclosed on any opened page. Related earlier Lucknow seizures: Rs 21 lakh fake allopathic medicines from an illegal Aminabad warehouse (19 July 2026) and approx Rs 1.6 lakh near Alambagh Metro Station (6 July 2026). Saharanpur follow-up (2 Sept 2026): approx 32.555 kg drug strips, 973 printed cartons of Difcort-6, 472 printed cartons of Rosuvas F-10, approx 6.950 kg yellow pills, 4.900 kg white pills, approx 6.370 kg plain aluminium foil, stripping machines, batch stereos, die-punches - sealed in 15 sacks on Form-16; no rupee value given.

Ejaz/Aijaz Ahmed of Saharanpur arrested by Lucknow SOG and police in the Aminabad case (reported 2 Sept 2026); his interrogation led to the Saharanpur Nagal packing-unit raid. FSDA suspended operations and sealed nine Aminabad wholesale establishments (SKG Medicals, Gayatri Pharma & Surgical, Health Plus, MK Pharma, Maa Ambe Pharma, RN Pharma, Sunlight Pharma, Sonal Pharma, Supervision Pharma) pending examination of financial/billing records under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act (Medical Dialogues 2 Aug). No chargesheet, bail or licence-cancellation order reported on opened pages; other arrests not reported.

cases.case_title: CBN Operation Vajra: Gaya/Masaurhi (Patna) counterfeit medicine and narcotics network; 8 godowns sealed, Masaurhi farmhouse manufacturing unit dismantled, mastermind arrested
cases.city: Gaya (Khanjahanpur / Manpur-Buniyadganj, Murarpur) and Masaurhi (Patna district)
cases.agency: Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Madhya Pradesh Unit, Neemuch (Preventive Section) under 'Operation Vajra'; follow-up seizures and sealed godowns handed to State Drug Administration of Bihar (Gaya District Drug Controller Dr. Sachchidanand Vikram per Jagran); joint searches with local police (Buniyadganj and Kotwali police station areas), State Drug Department and Food Department; announced by PIB (Ministry of Finance) release ID 2293146 on 01 Aug 2026
cases.fir_details: No FIR number reported. CBN case is a follow-up to a CBN crime registered in 2025 (May 2025 per Times of India) in which four illegal godowns in Gaya yielded 68,200 Tramadol tablets, 59,000 other tablets and 52,542 bottles of Codeine syrup. Machinery and materials at the Masaurhi farmhouse unit seized under the NDPS Act, 1985. Non-NDPS counterfeit stock and sealed godowns handed to the State Drug Administration of Bihar for action (Drugs and Cosmetics Act action implied; samples sent for laboratory testing per Jagran).
cases.seizure_value_inr: Not stated by CBN/PIB. Jagran (27 Jul 2026): approx Rs 2.50 crore of suspected medicines recovered in the 23-27 July joint CBN/district drug administration operation in Gaya (approx Rs 17.50 lakh from four Murarpur godowns; approx Rs 50 lakh earlier from Manpur/Buniyadganj). Deshaj Times: 'crores of rupees' (unquantified).
cases.status: Main accused (mastermind, absconding since the 2025 CBN case) arrested by CBN on 22 July 2026; an associate 'arrested earlier' ran the Masaurhi farmhouse unit. Surveillance/field operations 16-27 July 2026. Two godowns in Khanjahanpur, Gaya searched (21,373 unauthorised Buprenorphine injection ampoules plus counterfeit Clavam-625, PAN-40, Betadine Ointment, Azithral etc.), six more unregistered godowns identified with local police (total 8 godowns sealed); illicit manufacturing unit at farmhouse near Masaurhi, Patna dismantled and machinery seized under NDPS Act. cases.status: Kingpin Surendra Gupta (Shri Medical Agency, Kambutola) arrested by Kotwali police from his residence on Saturday 18 Jul 2026; other accused in that FIR being searched for and have moved court for bail (Amar Ujala, 19 Jul 2026). cases.case_title: Delhi Mukherjee Nagar inter-state spurious/relabelled medicine racket (Rs 6 crore seizure incl. counterfeit Abhayrab rabies vaccine batch KE25012); 4 arrested by Crime Branch; CDL Kasauli NSQ+misbranded; DCGI alert to states 27 Aug 2026, CDSCO public notice 5 Sep 2026
cases.state: Delhi (sourcing from government hospitals/CHCs in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh; counterfeit human albumin unit at Dera Bassi, Punjab; sales network Delhi-NCR, Kolkata/West Bengal, Guwahati/Assam, Imphal/Manipur and other Northeast locations)

cases.agency: Crime Branch, Delhi Police (Eastern Range-I unit; raid led by Inspector Lichman under ACP Sunil Srivastava and DCP (Crime) Pankaj Kumar) jointly with Drugs Inspectors of the Drugs Control Department, Govt of NCT of Delhi; CDSCO North Zone (Drugs Inspector P. Selvaraj) did legal sampling; Central Drugs Laboratory (CDL) Kasauli tested; DCGI Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi issued letter to all State Drugs Controllers dated 27 Aug 2026; CDSCO public notice 5 Sep 2026
cases.fir_details: FIR registered on 23 April 2026 at Crime Branch police station, Delhi, under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Drugs and Cosmetics Act (FIR number and specific sections not published in any opened page). CDSCO Drugs Inspector's sampling memorandum: NZ/SMP/PS-A/013/2026/466-67 dated 23 April 2026; CDL Kasauli test certificate (Form 13) CDL No. 2932/2026 - 30 vials of 0.5 mL received 11 May 2026; Government Analyst opinion: Not of Standard Quality and misbranded under Section 17 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, with advice to investigate applicability of Section 17B (spurious)
cases.seizure_value_inr: Approx. Rs 6 crore (Crime Branch Delhi Police, 7 May 2026) - medicines plus four packaging/labelling machines; Rs 10 crore figure appears only in NDTV-derived reports (Medical Dialogues, Madhyamam) and is not supported by the Crime Branch statement
cases.hospital_link: No hospital, clinic or hospital pharmacy was named as a recipient of the seized/relabelled stock. Direction of hospital link is upstream: police say government-supply medicines (marked 'Government Supply - Not for Sale') were sourced through contacts in government hospitals and community health centres in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh (Madhyamam alone says diverted from Central Government Health Scheme supplies). CDSCO/IIL state that vaccines administered at hospitals, clinics and government facilities or dispensed by licensed pharmacies come through the authorised chain and are unaffected; whether any counterfeit KE25012 vial reached patients remains unestablished. Genuine KE25012 (83,370 vials, released 7 Nov 2025 under CDL/2025/8392) went only through IIL's authorised distribution; IIL received healthcare-professional queries but no market complaints.
cases.status: 4 arrested (Manoj Kumar Jain apprehended at the premises on 22 Apr 2026; three associates in follow-up action); FIR at Crime Branch PS on 23 Apr 2026; bust announced 7 May 2026; CDL Kasauli report NSQ + misbranded (failed potency; passed sterility, moisture, thiomersal, identity); IIL submitted batch manufacturing/QC/reconciliation/distribution records to CDSCO 14 Aug 2026; DCGI letter to State Drugs Controllers 27 Aug 2026 asking strict vigilance over movement/distribution/availability of Abhayrab batch KE25012 and regulatory action; IIL/Human Biologicals Institute statement 4 Sep 2026 (vials not its product; 17 differences; representation to DCGI to trace source); CDSCO public notice 5 Sep 2026 ('further investigation and appropriate legal action are being undertaken'); financial/hawala probe underway; police said more arrests likely. No chargesheet, bail order or licence action found in any opened page as of 7 Oct 2026. No brand-owner helpline published; identifying features per CDL/IIL: apostrophe instead of comma after 'Rabies Vaccine', 'L Posteur' instead of 'L Pasteur', larger/mispositioned ® symbol, font/text-spacing, logo, artwork number, QR code not verifiable via GS1, cap colour, hologram, licence details, preservative concentration, diluent details, warning-box text

cases.case_title: Gurugram counterfeit Mounjaro KwikPen flat-based manufacturing racket (Avi Sharma, Mujammil Khan) - DD No.19 PS Sector-29
cases.city: Gurugram (interception near Super Mart I, DLF Phase 4; manufacturing flat Tower-1, Flat No.605, 6th floor, Pivotal Paradise, Sector-62; accused resident of Eldeco Tower, Sector-2, Sohna)
cases.agency: Drugs Control Officer, Gurugram (Haryana FDA / state drugs control) - DCOs Amandeep Chauhan and Mukesh Kumar - with Gurugram Police (Police Station Sector-29 and Police Post Chakkarpur); prosecution as a Drugs & Cosmetics Act complaint case through the Drugs Control Officer
cases.fir_details: No regular FIR: DD No.19 dated 19.04.2026, Police Station Sector-29, Gurugram. Case U/s 18(c), 18-A, 17B(d), 17B(e), 27(b)(ii), 27(d), 27(a), 27(c) Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 (per bail order Avi Sharma v State, CNR HRGR-01009799-2026, CIS BA-2573-2026). Media (medicaldialogues) cite s.17B, 27(a), 27(c); legalmaestros additionally claims BNS charges, which the court order does not list. Defence noted it is a complaint case and the complaint had not yet been filed as of 20.06.2026. Vehicle seized: Swift Dzire HR-55AU-3582.
cases.seizure_value_inr: Rs 56,15,847 (MRP of sampled Mounjaro KwikPen injections per court order; Tribune/India Today report ~Rs 56 lakh); initial media reports (PTI/Business Standard, Deccan Herald, ETV Bharat, medicaldialogues) cited ~Rs 70 lakh
cases.hospital_link: none reported (sold via B2B portal IndiaMART to online/private buyers; suspected routing via Bhagirath Palace, Delhi; India Today reports some shipments traced to Hyderabad; no hospital, clinic or hospital pharmacy named)
cases.status: Both accused arrested 19.04.2026 (Avi Sharma in custody since 19.04.2026). Regular bail application of Avi Sharma (u/s 483 BNSS) dismissed by Additional Sessions Judge Yashwinder Paul Singh, Gurugram, order dated 20.06.2026 (instituted 30.05.2026); Advocate Vipin Gupta for accused, DCO Amandeep Chauhan in person for State. No chargesheet/complaint filed as of 20.06.2026 (complaint case). Nationwide alert issued and batch numbers shared with health departments (numbers not disclosed). Over 260 seized pens confirmed spurious after side-by-side comparison with originals (drugscontrol.org). Eli Lilly India (Winselow Tucker, President & GM) confirmed on 30.04.2026 the products were not manufactured by Lilly and did not originate from its authorised supply chain, said most counterfeit stock recovered, issued patient advisory (contact mailbox_in-gps@lilly.com); Lilly tirzepatide brands in India: Mounjaro and Yurpeak.

cases.enrichment: New facts added: (1) Timeline — 10-12-2025 raid at Nagpur Golden Transport, Gogaon, Raipur on an unclaimed parcel sent from Indore whose invoice did not match contents; samples drawn in four parts and sent to the Drug Testing Laboratory, Kalibadi, Raipur; lab report dated 16-12-2025 declared all three drugs substandard and fake; FDA Chhattisgarh alerted CDSCO New Delhi and all district officers (helpline +91 9340597097). (2) Sarangarh raids on Saraswati Medical Store on 16 and 20 December 2025; on 20-12-2025 (Saturday) a joint Raipur-Raigarh FDA team searched operator Khemram Kesarwani/Bani's house and found a purpose-built illegal godown with approx. Rs 50 lakh of undocumented medicines; photos of the Gogaon-seized medicine found on his phone; special team formed on orders of Controller FDA Deepak Agrawal (दीपक अग्रवाल), with a team to be sent to Indore. (3) 13-04-2026 arrests of three accused (supplier Rochak Agrawal of Bijrasan Medicos, Indore; Surendra Kamnani of Prem Prakash Agency, Bhatapara; Khemraj Bani of Saraswati Medical Store, Sarangarh); produced in court, 14 days judicial custody. (4) Assistant Drugs Controller Raipur Sanjay Kumar Netam suspended, departmental inquiry opened, after a viral video of his meeting with a Sarangarh medical operator. (5) Labelled manufacturers of the fake/NSQ drugs: M/s G Biotech Pvt Ltd (Nahan Road, Solan, HP), M/s G.C. Health Care (Solan, HP), M/s Lar Ox Pharmaceuticals (Chennai) — Latin spellings transliterated from Hindi. Still missing: brand/generic names of the antibiotics, batch numbers, FIR number/police station/sections, and any chargesheet or bail update after April 2026. Leads not opened (Google News RSS titles only, links could not be decoded due to rate limiting): Dainik Bhaskar 14-04-2026 "नकली दवाइयों के कारोबार से जुड़े तीन आरोपी गिरफ्तार: 4 महीने से थी तलाश", The Sootr 14-04-2026 "इंदौर से रायपुर तक फैला नकली दवाओं का नेटवर्क; पाउडर भरकर बेची जा रही दवाइयां", IBC24 14-04-2026 "CG Fake Medicine Racket: इंदौर से लाकर राजधानी के मेडिकल में खपा रहे थे". The DrugsControl full text (behind login) likely names the antibiotic brands.

cases.case_title: Delhi Police Crime Branch (Cyber Cell) interstate spurious Schedule-H medicines racket run from Bhagirath Palace wholesale shop with Rs 50 crore fake GST billing network (Nikhil Arora alias Sunny); illegal unit at Muzaffarnagar
cases.city: Delhi (Bihari Colony, Shahdara; Bhagirath Palace, Chandni Chowk); Muzaffarnagar (UP); Roorkee (Uttarakhand)
cases.agency: Delhi Police Crime Branch, Cyber Cell (DCP Crime Branch Aditya Gautam briefed media at police headquarters on Sunday 5 Apr 2026); first raid 11 Mar 2026 at Bihari Colony, Shahdara
cases.fir_details: FIR number and police station not reported in any opened page. Republic World (single source) states an FIR was registered under relevant sections of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, IPC and the Trade Marks Act. Separate prior cases: Mayank Aggarwal has NCB case(s) (booked by NCB in 2013 per BW Police World) and a recent FIR in Uttar Pradesh under drugs and cosmetics provisions (Tribune/PTI copy).
cases.seizure_value_inr: approx Rs 2 crore (counterfeit drugs); over 1.2 lakh counterfeit tablets/capsules (1,20,535 per BW Police World; over 20,000 units at the 11 Mar Shahdara raid per DCP Gautam/ETV Bharat); about 2,000 kg raw material (Metformin HCL, calcium carbonate, lactose, starch, magnesium stearate) plus tablet compression, coating, capsule filling, blister packaging and testing machinery and 10,000 empty falsely-labelled bottles at the Muzaffarnagar unit; 40,000 fake tablets buried in a UP village by Shivam and Mayank later dug out by police (BW Police World); fake GST invoices approx Rs 50 crore
cases.hospital_link: none reported in the seven primary sources. Supply chain described as manufacturer -> wholesalers -> retailers across Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh; retail shopkeepers who stocked the fake medicines were yet to be interrogated (ETV Bharat). Republic World alone mentions a hospital insider and diverted government-hospital medicines (Meropenem, Ceftriaxone, Rabies Antiserum, Rs 70 lakh, five arrested) but this conflicts with every other report and its own headline and appears to conflate another case; treated as unconfirmed.
cases.status: 6 arrested (Nikhil Arora alias Sunny, Shivam Tyagi, Mayank Aggarwal, Mohit Kumar Sharma, Shahrukh, Rahul); Muzaffarnagar unit operator Mohammad Aqdas Siddiqui absconding; gang said to be active 14-15 years, supplying Delhi, UP, Punjab, HP and MP; further arrests anticipated, investigation ongoing. No chargesheet, bail or licence-action reporting found as of 2026-10-07.

Nikhil Arora aged 47, shop identified as Baba Shyam Medicos, Bhagirath Palace, Chandni Chowk; his Shahdara house rooftop stored the stock; annual turnover Rs 3.5-5 crore. Exact seizure count 1,20,535 counterfeit tablets (BW Police World); over 20,000 units at the first raid. Distribution to Delhi, UP, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh via wholesalers then retailers; sold at 20-25% of market price with >100% margin; retail shopkeepers yet to be questioned; further arrests anticipated. cases.city: Dombivli East (Thane district; Manpada police, Thane Zone III) and Kandivali East, Mumbai
cases.date: 2026-01-20 (FDA raid at Shri Ram Pharma, per Newsband); FIR at Manpada PS and arrest of Pankaj Upadhyay followed; Vivek Rai arrested 2026-02-16; reported 2026-02-18/19
cases.agency: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) - inspector Rajshree Shinde conducted the raid on a complaint forwarded from Glenmark company officials; Manpada police (Thane), probe supervised by DCP Atul Zende (Zone III), ACP Suhas Hemade, Senior PI Sandipan Shinde, with API/Sub-Inspector Mahesh Ralebhat and the Crime Detection Team. Related but unlinked: CDSCO monthly spurious-drug alerts (Jul-2025, Oct-2025, Nov-2025, Dec-2025) list purported-spurious Telma AM / Telma 40 / Telma H batches with manufacturer 'Under Investigation'
cases.fir_details: FIR registered at Manpada Police Station (Thane) on the FDA's complaint, under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita along with provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules, 1945 (FPJ). FIR number and specific sections not reported in any opened page
cases.seizure_value_inr: Rs 8,94,400 (2,795 strips of Telma AM, Telmisartan 40 mg + Amlodipine 5 mg IP) per Free Press Journal (two reports) and Newsband; Medical Dialogues reports 'around 1,000 strips' seized at the Dombivli distributor
cases.status: Two arrested (Pankaj Upadhyay taken into custody after FIR; Vivek Rai arrested 2026-02-16). Upadhyay claimed to have sourced 6,000 strips from a Bihar-based pharmaceutical company; police found the claim false and the invoice fabricated. Probe expanded to trace the main supplier/manufacturing unit and a suspected interstate (Bihar-linked) network using fake invoices across states. No chargesheet, bail order or licence suspension/cancellation found in any opened page (latest coverage 2026-02-19). CDSCO Telma batch listings remain 'Under Investigation'

cases.enrichment: New facts: kingpin Pramod Kumar Gupta (67) arrested 16 Dec 2025 at Hazrat Nizamuddin railway station after Shree Ram disclosed his role as supplier/key conspirator; Gupta ran an illegal unit in a rented farmhouse at Bijwasan village, southwest Delhi, where police seized ~600 kg stearic acid, machines, empty boxes and ~800 boxes each of counterfeit Fair and Lovely and Veet hair removal cream (HUL representative confirmed fake); Gupta allegedly burnt ~25 cartons (~27,000 tubes) of spurious Betnovate-C and fled to another state after an associate's arrest; he has a 2006 Copyright Act case at Sadar Bazar PS. FIR registered 12 Dec 2025 at Crime Branch PS, Delhi, under BNS and Drugs and Cosmetics Act. Operation sequence: first raid at Teliwara, Sadar Bazar (large wholesale pharma/cosmetic market) where Schedule-H counterfeit ointments were recovered; technical analysis and interrogation led to the Loni factory raided on the night of 13 Dec 2025 (seizure: ~1,200 Betnovate-C tubes, 2,700+ Clop-G tubes, 3,700+ Skin-Shine tubes, ~22,000 empty fake Clop-G tubes, 350+ kg semi-prepared ointment, chemicals and mixing/filling/sealing machinery; ETV: 5,400 tubes of a reputed firm's brand plus 22,000 empty tubes and 350 kg raw material; Akashvani: over 7,500 counterfeit ointments). Drug inspectors from North and Central Zones of Delhi and UP plus company representatives drew samples and confirmed the products were not made or supplied by the brand owners; accused held no manufacturing/storage/sale licence. Racket ran ~6 years; Gaurav Bhagat and Vishal Gupta are Class 8 dropouts; Gaurav learnt the process from YouTube, bought machinery at Anand Parvat; production cost Rs 1.50-2 per tube, sold to wholesalers at ~Rs 15, retail Rs 70-100; raw materials sourced from several states; ~358 kg spurious medicines seized; police exploring attachment of assets acquired from profits (Medical Dialogues citing Amar Ujala). Not found: FIR number, specific BNS sections, batch numbers on seized tubes, hospital names, chargesheet or bail updates (2 extended WebSearch calls returned nothing beyond Dec-2025 coverage). Unlinked observation: CDSCO Feb-2026 alert lists Betamethasone and Clioquinol Cream BP batch K73G and Clobetasol Propionate & Gentamicin Sulphate Cream batch IA00187A (both CDL Kolkata, manufacturer 'Under Investigation', label-claim manufacturers deny making them) - no page connects these to the Delhi/Loni case. Earlier prosecutions: 2015 ADC Dharwad Circle, Hubballi (Karnataka) case vs Goyal and sons (quash plea rejected by Karnataka HC Dharwad bench); 2022 case by ADC Shwetha Nagathan, Vijayapura Circle (spurious pantoprazole); 2023 Port Blair case by Drug Inspector Deepak Shetty, CDSCO East Zone Kolkata (quashed by Calcutta HC in 2024).
cases.seizure_value_inr: Rs 574 crore (NCB, per TNM/Newslaundry Apr 2026); reported as 'over Rs 547 crore' (Medical Dialogues, 2025-11-10) and 'around Rs 600 crore' (The Tribune, 2025-11-29/30 and 2026-02-20). Seizures: 34 lakh psychotropic tablets, 10.57 lakh bottles codeine-based cough syrup, 1,613 kg psychotropic raw material, 573 kg tramadol bulk mixture, 50,000 tramadol ampoules, 5,000 midazolam vials; NCB says over 60% of seized material linked to Digital Vision
cases.hospital_link: none reported. Diverted drugs went to fictitious distributor firms (Tiwari Medical Agencies, Dehradun; Rama Medicose and Maa Jagdamba Medicose, Jodhpur), not hospitals. cases.status: Ongoing. NCB case: 15 arrested as of 2025-11-30 (The Tribune), 17 arrested per TNM/Newslaundry 2026-04-13; partner Anuj Kumar Singh arrested 2025-11-01 (five-day police custody); Parshotam Lal Goyal and sons absconding since August 2025 with non-bailable warrants; Punjab and Haryana HC dismissed Goyal's anticipatory bail plea on 2026-02-16 (15th rejection). HP drug authorities issued 'stop manufacturing' order on 2025-11-05 (uncalibrated equipment, air-handling lapses). Vellinton Healthcare MD-VI licence revoked Nov 2024; review rejected; Vellinton debarred by Armed Forces Medical Services Jan 2025 until Jan 2027. DEG case: owners got anticipatory bail from J&K HC 2020-04-20 (bond Rs 50,000); manufacturing licence suspended 2020-03-02, blanket suspension set aside by HP HC June 2020 (ban only on the two syrups); chargesheet 2023-02-28, 24 hearings, latest 2026-01-14; Feb 2024 further-investigation order stayed by J&K HC. No one from the company has been jailed for the deaths; NHRC-ordered Rs 3 lakh compensation to 12 of 16 families upheld by Supreme Court.

Ongoing.

cases.case_title: UP FSDA Aug 2026: Rs 5.43 crore fake/illegal medicines seized in Lucknow, Agra, Varanasi, Gonda; Aminabad fake-billing syndicate booked, interstate counterfeit factory raided
cases.city: Lucknow (Aminabad, Alambagh, Bakshi Ka Talab, Kaisarbagh), Agra, Varanasi (Manduadih), Gonda (Badgaon); linked raids in Meerut, Baghpat, Saharanpur, Ghaziabad, Udham Singh Nagar and Dehradun (Uttarakhand)
cases.agency: UP Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) (Commissioner Dr Roshan Jacob; Joint Commissioner Brijesh Kumar quoted by ETV Bharat); Aminabad police station, Lucknow (FIR); joint team of UP FSDA, Crime Branch Ghaziabad and Uttarakhand Drug Department (illegal factory raid)
cases.fir_details: FIR number not reported. Aminabad police station, Lucknow, 12 Aug 2026, against the four Aminabad-network firms/operators under BNS sections 111, 276, 277, 278, 318, 319, 336 and 338 (Aaj Tak, ABP, Jagran, Bhaskar, NBT, Prabhat Khabar). Lucknow total: 7 FIRs against 32 persons; earlier FIR against 8 Aminabad firms and a software distributor for fake billing/software manipulation; Kaisarbagh cross-billing case under BNS. Agra: 9 FIRs against 15+ operators (Kambutola, Mubarak Mahal, Shoe Market, Nawabia Market per Jagran). Varanasi: shop operator booked under BNS 277, 278, 318(4). Gonda: action under Drugs and Cosmetics Act and NDPS Act. Illegal factory: FIR against two accused. Jagran also reports FIRs against Bhupendra Sharma and transporter Satendra Gujjar (Rajasthan-sourced stock of Aminabad godown) and against Rajendra Singh alias Arun Tunda, Vinay Bhatnagar, Gaurav Tyagi and Vinay Chandra (Dehradun illegal manufacturing unit).
cases.seizure_value_inr: Rs 5.43 crore total (Lucknow Rs 41.58 lakh; Agra Rs 3.63 crore; Gonda Rs 1.13 crore; Varanasi Rs 25 lakh). Separately: Rs 2 crore medicines, machinery and packaging at the illegal factory; Rs 1.88 crore fake billing detected in Agra; Rs 8.87 crore fake purchases shown by MK Pharma in FY 2025-26
cases.hospital_link: No hospital or clinic named as having received counterfeit stock. Agra raids found medicines supplied for hospitals and government institutions (government-quota Zostum-O, ESI and defence supply, insulin and rabies vaccine) relabelled with new labels/arbitrary MRP and black-marketed (Jagran, Bhaskar, ABP, India Today); Jyoti Drug House held Rs 2.5 crore of insulin, vaccines and physician samples without cold chain.
cases.status: ongoing. Lucknow: 7 FIRs against 32 persons, 2 arrests; Agra: 9 FIRs, 2 arrests; Varanasi: surgical shop operator arrested on the spot; Gonda: main accused arrested, co-accused absconding; illegal factory: 2 accused booked. Commissioner Dr Roshan Jacob directed licence cancellation plus criminal action against traders found guilty; no specific cancellation order reported.

cases.enrichment: From Deccan Herald (27 Dec 2025, Kalyan Ray): ATAGI alert text - "Counterfeit batches of rabies vaccine Abhayrab have been circulating in India since November 2023"; advises people vaccinated with Abhayrab or unknown brand in India from 1 Nov 2023 to seek replacement doses with an Australian-registered vaccine. IIL (wholly owned subsidiary of National Dairy Development Board) in its Dec 25 reply called the reference to the March-2024 batch "over-cautionary and misplaced", said it proactively identified a packaging anomaly in one batch (No: KA24014) in January 2025, notified regulators and law enforcement, lodged a formal complaint; "This was an isolated incident, and the counterfeit batch is no longer available on the shelves"; asked ATAGI to review the advisory. After IIL alerted CDSCO in January, the Delhi government's Drugs Control Department issued a notice that the counterfeit was available in markets of Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Lucknow. IIL says it has supplied more than 210 million Abhayrab doses and holds ~40% of the national anti-rabies vaccine market. From All India Radio (27 Dec 2025): IIL said the alert "does not reflect the current situation" and that every batch is tested and released by the Central Drugs Laboratory. From TravelHealthPro (edited 26 Feb 2026): falsified Abhayrab first reported to DCGI by IIL on 13 January 2025; UK four-nation look-back for travellers who received rabies vaccine after an animal bite in India from 1 Nov 2023 to 22 Jan 2026; additional vaccination offered to some after individual risk assessment; no further evidence of continued circulation. From the linked Delhi Drugs Control Department PDF (drugscontrol.org): letter F.13(15)/Misc/HQ/2017/7198 dated 28/3/25 to Sh. Sandeep Nangia (President), Retail Distribution Chemist Alliance (RDCA), H-O-42 Lajpat Nagar, New Delhi, signed (K.R. Chawla), Head of Office/DDC/Controlling & Licensing Authority, forwarding a DCG(I)/CDSCO Enforcement Division letter on the counterfeit "Rabies Vaccine, Human (Abhayrab), Batch No. KA24014"; enclosed IIL/HBI letter HBIK/QM/RAB:2025/001 dated 13.01.2025 to DCGI signed Sunil Tiwari, VP & Head of Quality Management, HBI, giving original batch details (KA24014, Mfg 03/24, Exp 02/27, MRP 397.62; diluent Sodium Chloride Injection 0.9% w/v batch SCSVIA3123, Mfg 11/23, Exp 10/27) and counterfeit variations (Mfg 11/23, Exp 10/26, missing rupee symbol, different font; diluent Mfg 05/23, Exp 04/27), noting the counterfeit circulated without the 2-8 C cold chain, and urging CDSCO market surveillance, seizure and coordination with law enforcement. No arrests, FIR number, seizure value or hospital recipients are reported on any opened page.

cases.case_title: Respifresh TR (Rednex Pharmaceutical, Ahmedabad) and ReLife (Shape Pharma, Surendranagar) DEG-contaminated cough syrups; MP ban and recall; WHO Medical Product Alert N°5/2025
cases.state: Gujarat (manufacturers) / Madhya Pradesh (distribution, ban and recall)
cases.city: Bavla, Ahmedabad and Shekhpur, Surendranagar (Gujarat); Bhopal (MP drug market/MPFDA)
cases.agency: MPFDA (Madhya Pradesh Food and Drug Administration); CDSCO; relevant state authorities (production halt, suspension of product authorisations, recall); WHO (Medical Product Alert N°5/2025, 13 Oct 2025)
cases.fir_details: not reported
cases.seizure_value_inr: not reported
cases.hospital_link: none reported for Respifresh TR / ReLife. TOI: Respifresh (6,528 bottles) and Relife (1,400 bottles) distributed to 30 to 35 districts across Madhya Pradesh through the Bhopal drug market; drug inspectors directed to search medical shops and remove products. (AIIMS Nagpur is mentioned only as treating MP children who consumed toxic cough syrups; the 23 Chhindwara child deaths are linked to Coldrif, not these two brands.)

No FIR, arrests, chargesheet or licence-cancellation details reported for Rednex or Shape Pharma on the opened pages.

Full manufacturer addresses added. CDSCO reported the DEG presence to WHO on 8 Oct 2025 after WHO identified clusters of acute illness and child fatalities on 30 Sep 2025; state authorities ordered an immediate production halt at implicated sites, suspended product authorisations and initiated recall; CDSCO says none of the medicines were exported; WHO advises NRAs to evaluate oral liquids from the same sites produced since December 2024. From TOI (Bhopal, updated 11 Oct 2025): MP govt banned sale of Coldrif, Respifresh and Relife and initiated market recall; Respifresh 6,528 bottles and Relife 1,400 bottles reached 30 to 35 MP districts through the Bhopal drug market; MPFDA wrote to district collectors and directed drug inspectors to search medical shops; Coldrif (approx 660 bottles) was confined to Chhindwara and linked to 23 child deaths. No FIR numbers, arrests, chargesheet, bail or licence-cancellation details for Rednex or Shape Pharma were found on the opened pages; the CDSCO public-notices list (checked) carries no product-specific notice for these brands.

cases.enrichment: From CDSCO Jul-2025 NSQ table: 143 NSQ records - 46 'CDSCO Labs', 97 'State lab' (matches IndiaMedToday's 46/97 split). Jul-2025 spurious table: iTotalRecords 8; exact test failures and mfg/exp dates added per batch (Venclyxto exp Aug-2027, disintegration; Deca-Durabolin 50 G401852 mfg Jul-2024/exp Jun-2028; Thrombophob I403999 mfg Aug-2024/exp Jul-2027; Augmentin 824D269 mfg Sep-2024; Clavam 24441030 mfg Mar-2024/exp Aug-2025; PAN 40 23440679 mfg Feb-2023/exp Jul-2025; Telma H 18210121 mfg Sep-2023/exp Jul-2026 and 18230729 mfg Nov-2023/exp Oct-2026). IndiaMedToday (citing The Economic Times): Health Ministry said the eight batches were made by unauthorized producers using brand names of established companies; some fall within India's top 30 prescribed brands; CDSCO published the detailed list about a week after the Ministry alert, coinciding with launch of a new searchable NSQ portal (data back to 2019) - corroborated by the cdsco.gov.in alerts index entry 'Availability of Not Standard Quality (NSQ) Alert on New Link in CDSCO Website' dated 2025-Aug-28. May-2026 spurious tab has 2 rows: Medreich-labelled amoxyclav 825D167 and Blue Cross Laboratories-labelled Cefixime Dispersible Tablets IP TC2439 (mfg Oct-2024, exp Mar-2027; uniformity of dispersion, dissolution, assay), both CDL Kolkata, both 'Under Investigation'. Pattern context from Sep-2024 NSQ list: genuine Alkem Health Science (Unit-2, Samardung, South Sikkim) batches of CLAVAM 625 (23443940) and PAN 40 (22442076) were NSQ at RDTL Guwahati - these are NSQ, not spurious, and confirm Alkem as the real maker of those brands only indirectly, so not added to firms. May-2025 NSQ list also carries two 'Telma 40' batches (5240226, K18230707) with manufacturer 'Under Investigation' at CDL Kolkata - possible earlier spurious Telma pattern. No FIR number, police station, seizure value, accused persons, or hospital/pharmacy distribution appears on any opened page.

cases.status: Advisory to all pharmacists being prepared after a high-level state Health Department meeting (reported 7 Apr 2025): any wholesale medicine supplier or pharmacist found selling fake medicines to have licence cancelled; medicine shops to display QR codes of medicines; Directorate of Drug Control helpline 033 2225-2213 / 033 2225-2214 published for public reports. Follow-up: on Friday 23 May 2025 (reported 24 May 2025) the West Bengal Drug Control department issued six guidelines for drug sellers and wholesalers (verify distribution channel from the original company, check seller licence validity on online licence portal and submit outside-state distributor details to WB drug control for verification, pay outside-state wholesalers only into bank accounts in the licensed firm's name, check GST number and GST credit, wholesalers and retailers must check QR codes of the 300 Schedule H2 drugs). WB government had earlier (31 Mar 2025) sought cooperation of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh governments in investigating spurious drugs recovered in North 24 Parganas and Malda, stating many were made in those states. In the Amta (Howrah) case the agency office was sealed and its owner arrested.

cases.enrichment: Confirmed from the CDSCO 'List of Drugs, Medical Devices, Vaccine and Cosmetics declared as Spurious for the Month of February-2025' (posted 2025-Mar-29): Telma H (Telmisartan 40mg & Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg), batch 05240198, Mfg Feb-2024, Exp Jan-2027, Manufactured By 'Under Investigation', reason 'Does not Conform to I.P.', Drawn By '-', firm's reply that the batch was not manufactured by them and is spurious, remark that it is subject to outcome of investigation. Added batch numbers, dates, NSQ results and testing lab (CDL, Kolkata) for the NSQ products from the CDSCO NSQ Alert Feb-2025 PDF and the cdscoonline.gov.in NSQ table (103 records for FEB-2025: 47 CDSCO lab, 56 State lab): Eurolife Ringer Lactate DCSL3021; Martin & Brown Rabeprazole Tablets MT-24E30, Rabeprazole Sodium Injection MD23H10 and MD24E30, Aminophylline MA23L108, CMC Eye Drops MO24H19, Polywin MA24H16; Health Biotech Adrenaline Bitartrate HIAN24005A and Bupivacaine HIBU23010; Higgs Healthcare Hi-Ring-RL F41746/F41799. South First (30 Mar 2025) corroborates Telma H batch 05240198 spurious, 103 NSQ (47 central/56 state), and notes Telma AM by the same manufacturer was NSQ the previous month; South First (22 Jun 2025) records later Telma 40 spurious batches 5240226 (March-2025 alert) and 05240226/K18230707 (May-2025 alert, drawn by a Drugs Inspector in Bihar), showing a recurring pattern on the Telma brand. The cdscoonline spurious table currently holds only the latest month (Aug-2026), so no later status change for batch 05240198 is visible; no FIR, licence action or hospital supply reported anywhere. The correct Medical Dialogues article for this alert is titled 'Drug Alert: 47 Drug Samples Fail To Clear CDSCO Test, 1 Declared spurious' (31 Mar 2025) but its real URL/ID could not be resolved (Google News redirect only); the Business Standard story 'Spurious batch of Telma H flagged, 103 other drugs fail CDSCO tests' dated 30 Mar 2025 exists per Google News RSS but the given URL now serves the April article.

cases.case_title: Reference: hospital pharmacy stock verification guidance
cases.agency: CDSCO / DCGI; Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC); Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration (FDA); Telangana Drugs Control Administration (DCA); Haryana drug control authority; brand owners (Pfizer India, Indian Immunologicals / Human Biologicals Institute, Torrent, Abbott, Glenmark, Eli Lilly India, Mankind)
cases.fir_details: not applicable (reference entry). Underlying Karnataka case: criminal case registered under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 after the 18 Aug 2026 Bidadi raid; seized stock to be produced before the JMFC Court, Bengaluru South; SIT under IPS officer C Vamsi Krishna (Deccan Herald 20 Sep 2026, Hans India 21 Sep 2026). Underlying Delhi Abhayrab case: four persons arrested by Delhi Police (CDSCO public notice quoted by Indian Express, 6 Sep 2026).
cases.seizure_value_inr: not applicable (reference entry). Karnataka Bidadi raid: Rs 5.05 crore (inventory value Rs 4.91 crore) per Hans India; 'over Rs 5 crore' per Deccan Herald.
cases.hospital_link: Practical verification pointers for hospital pharmacies, each now checked against an opened page: (1) CDSCO's monthly 'Spurious' tab on cdscoonline.gov.in (filteredSpuriousDrugTable?month=MMM-YYYY&tab=spurious) records for each row the brand owner's reply 'The actual manufacturer (as per label claim) has informed that the impugned batch of the product has not been manufactured by them and that it is a spurious drug' - Dec-2025 table opened: 10 rows (Chymoral Forte 2KU6L012 and 2KU6L045; Montina-L SPJ241236; Zerodol-SP FND072001BH and FND0725001BH; Telma-AM 05241038A and 18240626; Telma 40 18240413; Defcort 6 13240334A; Pantop-D SR SPA250021). (2) Karnataka FDA 'has blocked the batch numbers and entries of the seized medicines on the Karnataka FDA portal to prevent their further sale or distribution' and samples sent for lab testing (Hans India, Deccan Herald) - hospitals should obtain that blocked-batch list from the state drug controller; the opened pages do not say the list was circulated to all states. (3) Pfizer India statement (reported 'late on Tuesday evening' in ETPharma article of 24 Sep 2026, i.e. 22 Sep 2026; also carried by Deccan Herald): 'removing from the market Pfizer batches (where batch numbers were copied by counterfeit) to avoid confusion, supporting to differentiate between original and counterfeit product, and providing technical and other relevant information related to the affected batches' - affected batch numbers are not published on the opened pages. (4) Human Biologicals Institute (division of Indian Immunologicals Ltd) statement dated 4 Sep 2026: the CDL Kasauli report documented 17 differences between the Delhi-seized Abhayrab vial (Batch No. KE25012, seized from an unlicensed residential premises in Mukherjee Nagar, Delhi) and CDL's retained samples; genuine KE25012 was released under Batch Release Certificate No. CDL/2025/8392 dated 7 Nov 2025, 83,370 vials, supplied exclusively through authorised distribution; IIL says vaccines reaching hospitals/clinics via the authorised supply chain are not affected. Indian Express (6 Sep 2026) lists the packaging tells: apostrophe instead of comma, 'L Pasteur' spelled 'L Posteur', font/text-spacing changes, different company logo; DCGI communication dated 27 Aug 2026 asked all State Drugs Controllers to watch the batch; the batch was never exported. (5) Karnataka FDA: 'counterfeit labels featured QR codes that were completely non-functional upon verification' (Deccan Herald); the department asks that non-scanning QR codes be reported to Drug Enforcement authorities (Hans India) - a QR code that does not resolve is a red flag. (6) Counter-example: fake Sun Pharma Levipil 500 (Batch No. GTF1540A, seized in Hyderabad and Karimnagar, Telangana; also found in Gujarat) carried active QR codes that falsely authenticated the product (Pharmacy Pro, 15 Jul 2025) - a resolving QR code is not proof of genuineness. Hospital-type licensees named in the Karnataka action: St Philomena Hospital Drug Centre, Vinayak Nagar (licence cancelled) and Surya Speciality Hospital, Bommasandra Industrial Area (licence suspended) per Deccan Herald; no hospital is named as a recipient of specific counterfeit batches on the opened pages.
cases.status: Reference entry (ongoing). Verified status points: Karnataka FDA cancelled 16 and suspended 8 drug licences (announced Sunday 20 Sep 2026), including suspension of M/s Pfizer C&F Depot, Kempalinganahalli (DH spelling: Kempanalinganahalli), Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural; SIT probing supply chain across six states. drugscontrol.org headline list (6-7 Oct 2026, headline only, article behind login): 'Karnataka High Court stays FSDA licence cancellation of Fortune Medical Solutions, suspension of Vivanta Pharmaceuticals' and 'SIT Raids Three Bengaluru Pharmacies, Traces Trail of Fake Medicine Sales'. No dedicated 2025-26 public counterfeit notice with helpline from Roche, MSD, GSK, Novo Nordisk, Cipla or Dr Reddy's appears on any opened page (CDSCO Latest-Alerts lists only an 'Alert on theft of multiple drug products of M/s. Novo Nordisk during transit', 21 Aug 2025). Lilly India toll-free helpline 1800 123 0021 / mailbox_in-gps@lilly.com (Pragativadi, 1 May 2026).

products.brand: Top-300 brands under Schedule H2 / expanded QR mandate
products.issue: Drugs Rules, 1945 amended to require a bar code or QR code on primary (or secondary) packaging of vaccines, antimicrobials, anti-cancer drugs and NDPS drugs, extending the existing top-300-brand rule; code must store nine data elements: unique product identification code, proper and generic name, brand name, manufacturer name and address, batch number, date of manufacture, date of expiry, manufacturing licence number, excipients; effective 1 July 2027 for most categories, antimicrobials by 1 July 2028 (Outlook India, 29 Jun 2026). Missing/unscannable/mismatched code is a red flag.

(3) DCC meeting 18 Sep 2026: Rajasthan raised disposal of machinery from closed/non-compliant pharma units; DCC asked Drug Controller Rajasthan for detailed proposal covering identification, manufacture/supply, ownership, transfer, decommissioning and disposal of pharma machinery; NHRC recommendations (centralised medicine registration, real-time tracking portal, dynamic QR codes) sent to DCC (Business Standard, 1-2 Oct 2026). UNSUPPORTED AND REMOVED: draft DMDC Bill 2026 '10 yrs-life' clause, 'Syrup' omitted from Schedule K (Jun 2026), Centre weighing central licensing of sterile drugs, Himachal Pradesh HC ruling on CDSCO inspectors - none appear on any opened page.
cases.enrichment: Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026: Bill No. 104-F of 2026; passed Lok Sabha 1 Apr 2026, Rajya Sabha 2 Apr 2026; assent 7 Apr 2026; Gazette of India Extraordinary Part II Sec 1 No. 13, New Delhi 8 Apr 2026 (CG-DL-E-08042026-271642); Act No. 8 of 2026; amends 80 central Acts; comes into force on notification. Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 entry (Schedule item 8) seen in Act text: s.27A(ii) cosmetics offence (imprisonment up to 1 yr / fine Rs 20,000) replaced with 'penalty of one lakh rupees or three times the value of the cosmetics confiscated, whichever is higher'; s.28A replaced with penalty 'not less than three lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees'; s.29 omitted; s.30(1A),(2) omitted; new s.30A adjudication by officer not below Deputy/Assistant Drugs Controller with appeal within 30 days and disposal in 60 days; s.32B and s.33 consequential; s.33-I(2) amended. Section 27 (spurious/adulterated drug penalties) is not among the listed amendments (A)-(H) seen. The PRS Bill Track also notes fines/penalties rise 10% of minimum every three years. SC PIL: respondents MoHFW, Law and Justice, Women and Child Development, all states/UTs, Law Commission; seeks SOPs for search/seizure/sampling, time-bound forensic examination, mandatory videography, graded sentencing policy, Law Commission report; cites Article 21; references alleged fake cancer drugs supplied to Bengaluru hospitals and cough-syrup deaths. DCC 18 Sep 2026 (per minutes reviewed by Business Standard, reporter Sanket Koul, first published 1 Oct 2026, updated 2 Oct 2026): DCC observed implementation of any such framework 'seems to be very poor' and that a mechanism 'would have to cover the wider supply chain of pharmaceutical machinery'; Drug Controller Rajasthan to submit proposal incl. monitoring, resource implications, scrap monitoring; NHRC recommendations (centralised registration, real-time supply-chain tracking portal, dynamic QR codes) sent to DCC; context: at least seven women died in Kota and Bikaner from spurious oxytocin injections post-partum, Rajasthan cancelled licence of an unnamed Kota-based distributor.
